key_insight: ChatGPT responses were broadly consistent with chiropractic guidelines, but college-level readability and poor rater agreement temper the findings.
clinical_relevance: LLM-generated chiropractic education may need simpler language and clinician review before patient-facing use.
method: Developed 30 questions on low back, neck, and chronic musculoskeletal pain using U.S. chiropractic guidelines.
Generated GPT-5.2 responses in isolated sessions and assessed readability.
Five licensed chiropractors independently rated relevance, clarity, completeness, and accuracy on 5-point scales.
evidence_signal: Mean ratings ranged from 4.00/5 for accuracy to 4.76/5 for clarity, while ordinal Krippendorff’s alpha ranged from −0.023 to 0.214, indicating poor inter-rater reliability.
watch_item: High average ratings do not establish dependable clinical accuracy, particularly given poor rater agreement and evaluation of only 30 questions.
paper_title: Evaluating ChatGPTs Responses to Chiropractic Patient Questions: A Comparative Study
